subject: Hosted→Dedicated: proposed credit taper, commit offsets & throughput SLAs
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@atlasai.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: AtlasAI Procurement <procurement@atlasai.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated migration — conversion credits / bridge months / SLA questions

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week. The leadership team at AtlasAI is ready to consider a Dedicated (reserved) commitment, but we need clarity on three items before we move to legal:

1) Conversion credits: can Redwood offset committed spend when we move our hosted usage to Dedicated? If so, how are those credits sized and do they taper?
2) Bridge months: our fiscal quarter ends Aug 31. We need a one-month overlap where some traffic remains on hosted while Dedicated ramps. Will you provide a bridge-month pricing model?
3) Throughput guarantees: we need a commitment that Dedicated will meet our peak inference throughput for our primary model (P98/99 latency and 95th percentile throughput).

Attached is a current SOW draft and a sample traffic snapshot for June. High level: we expect to migrate ~1.8B tokens/month today with peak bursts to ~650 tokens/sec sustained for 10–20 minute windows.

Can you outline a concrete proposal including: conversion credit schedule (months & %), commit offsets for existing credits, and a target SLA/measure for throughput? We’ll share this with procurement.

Best,
Priya
Priya Shah
Head of Infrastructure
AtlasAI

Attachments: AtlasAI_SOW_Draft_v3.pdf (SOW draft), traffic_snapshot_june.csv (attached)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@atlasai.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 13:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated migration — conversion credits / bridge months / SLA questions

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear ask and the SOW. High-level proposal below so you have something to review with procurement:

- Conversion credits: we offer a time-limited credit that converts a portion of your historical hosted spend into a Dedicated credit applied against the committed monthly invoice. For AtlasAI we can do: 2.0x months of your average committed monthly hosted spend as a credit pool, applied over the first 4 billing cycles with a taper (50% in month 1, 25% in month 2, 15% in month 3, 10% in month 4). Credits are conditional on signing a 12-month committed capacity agreement.

- Bridge month: we can provide one (1) complimentary bridge month where traffic split is tolerated (hosted+dedicated). During the bridge month we’ll bill hosted usage at current hosted rates (no uplift) and apply credits to Dedicated invoices as above. If AtlasAI needs two bridge months we can do so but the second month is billable at a 50% discounted hosted rate.

- Commit offsets & sizing: based on the traffic snapshot, recommended starting pool is 8x H100-similar GPUs (equiv. 8 L4-class nodes in our catalog) to meet your peak sustained bursts. We’ll include a capacity buffer to maintain throughput with autoscaling (burst pool). The commit offsets (the mapping from tokens/month to committed GPU units) are in the attached draft commit_schedule.

- Throughput SLA: proposed measurable target is: 99th percentile request completion within 300ms for inference requests up to 2k tokens and a sustained throughput floor of 600 tokens/sec across the pool during peak windows. SLA remedies are credit-based (service credit % of monthly invoice for sustained miss >2 consecutive hours).

Next steps: can you confirm a) target commit term (12 vs 24 months), b) whether the one free bridge month is sufficient, and c) whether legal should receive the SOW+DPA now. I’ve attached a baseline commit_schedule spreadsheet to show how credits map to monthly invoices.

Thanks — I’ll loop in finance/solutions for final approval if you’re broadly aligned.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 08:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated migration — conversion credits / bridge months / SLA questions

Laur, Marissa — forwarding Priya’s ask and my draft terms. Need quick approval/edits before I send the customer a formal term sheet. Key points I want to lock:

- Give AtlasAI a 2.0x-month credit pool applied over 4 months with the taper (50/25/15/10).
- One complimentary bridge month (second bridge at 50% hosted rate if needed).
- 12-month commit with a 20% off list price discount on committed units; default autoscaling burst pool billable at host rates.
- Throughput SLA: P99 latency target 300ms for requests <=2k tokens; sustained throughput floor 600 tokens/sec. Remedies = service credits.

Questions: is the 2.0x credit pool too generous? Can we condition the full-credit pool on a minimum committed spend (e.g., commit >= $250k ARR)? Also, Marissa — any concerns about the P99 SLA wording and how we measure (should we use 5-minute windows or 1-hour windows)?

I’m aiming to get legal + procurement aligned so we can send a DocuSign term sheet by Friday.

— Rishi

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated migration — conversion credits / bridge months / SLA questions

Sounds reasonable — quick notes:

- Credit pool: ok to do 2.0x months but require a minimum committed ARR of $275k to unlock full pool. If they sign for 24 months drop min to $200k.
- Bridge month: one complimentary bridge month is fine; second month at a 25% discounted hosted rate (not 50%).
- Discount: 20% off list is OK for 12m; for 24m make it 27.5% (we want to incentivize term).
- SLA: prefer measuring P99 on 5-minute rolling windows aggregated per cluster, with a 1-hour rolling remediation trigger. Avoid open-ended credits; cap cumulative service credits at 20% of monthly invoice.

Marissa — can you confirm finance is comfortable with those caps and minimums? If yes I’m good for Rishi to send a term sheet.

— Lauren

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Hi Priya — following internal alignment, here’s a concise term summary for AtlasAI. If the summary looks good I’ll send a formal DocuSign term sheet and SOW.

1) Conversion credit pool
   - Size: 2.0x months of AtlasAI’s average committed hosted monthly spend (credit pool amount will be calculated from your last 3 months of hosted invoices).
   - Schedule (tapered): Month 1 = 50% of pool applied; Month 2 = 25%; Month 3 = 15%; Month 4 = 10%.
   - Eligibility: requires 12-month committed Dedicated agreement. Minimum committed ARR to unlock full pool: $275,000 (we can lower to $200,000 if you choose 24-month term).

2) Bridge month(s)
   - One complimentary bridge month supported (traffic split allowed). If required, a second bridge month is available at 25% off current hosted rates.

3) Commit offsets & sizing
   - Recommended starting pool: 8 GPU-equivalent nodes (detailed mapping in attached commit_schedule_AtlasAI.xlsx).
   - Autoscaling: burst pool will be provisioned; burst usage billed at hosted rates unless covered by committed buffer.

4) Throughput SLA & remedies
   - Measurement: P99 latency measured on 5-minute rolling windows per cluster; remediation trigger = 1-hour sustained miss.
   - Target: 99th percentile request completion within 300ms for requests <= 2k tokens; sustained throughput floor 600 tokens/sec across the pool during peak windows.
   - Remedies: service credits; cumulative credits capped at 20% of the monthly invoice.

Next steps: confirm whether you want 12- or 24-month term, and whether the single complimentary bridge month is sufficient. If yes, I’ll circulate the DocuSign term sheet and the final SOW/DPA for signature.
